newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Sept 28 Initial Claims from 340,000, Sept 28 4-Week Average from 334,500, Sept 21 Continued Claims from 2,461,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial claims of 342,000 in the October 5 week.

The department said four states and Puerto Rico reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended September 28, the latest period for which the data are available.
They were North Carolina, with 4,591 fewer filings; Georgia, with 1,550; Florida, with 1,205; and South Carolina, with 1,098. Puerto Rico had 3,574 fewer claims.
North Carolina attributed the falloff in claims to fewer layoffs in the construction and textile industries.
Georgia linked the decrease to fewer layoffs in the textile and food industries, while South Carolina cited fewer layoffs in the food industry.
Florida reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, as well as in manufacturing and agriculture. Puerto Rico had no comment.

Tennessee, with 1,381 additional claims, was the only state reporting an increase in claims exceeding 1,000 in the week. It said increased claims activity was due to layoffs in the food, apparel, furniture, paper, fabricated metals, industrial machinery and electronic equipment industries.
